Consumer price index for consumer expenditures 2025=100
Price index, monthly and annual rate of change, weighting coefficient
value.ShortDescription:
This table contains figures on the Netherlands’ consumer price index (CPI). The CPI measures changes in the prices of goods and services purchased by households in the Netherlands for their own consumption. The table provides information about indices, monthly rates of change, annual rates of change and weighting coefficients. The annual rate of change of the CPI all items is known as the inflation. 

In addition to figures on total expenditure, figures on detailed product groups (expenditure categories) are also published. The table shows how much households in the Netherlands spend on each product group, on average, providing a picture of its share of total expenditure. This is also referred to as the weighting coefficient. The total weighting of the CPI is 100,000.

The table also shows the derived CPI. This is the CPI that excludes the effect of changes in the rates of product-related taxes (e.g., VAT or excise taxes). As such, the price index approximates what the price change would be if tax rates had remained the same.

CPI figures are published every month. After the end of each calendar year, annual figures are also released. The index figure for a given calendar year is calculated as the average of the indices for the twelve months in that year.

Data available from: December 2009.

Status of the figures:
Provisional figures for each reporting month are published in a flash estimate. The flash estimate includes monthly and annual rates of change in the total CPI and in a number of main groups (special aggregates). These figures are based on source data that is not yet complete and cannot be used for indexation purposes. Therefore, no indices are published in the flash estimate. The figures used for the flash estimate are provisional.

The flash estimate is followed by the first publication of indices and the rates of change across all expenditure categories. These figures are also provisional. The final figures for the same reporting month are published one month later. Any differences between the provisional and final figures are due to additional source data.

Changes compared to the previous version include: 
Data for a new period has been added and/or adjustments have been made.

When will new figures be published?
The flash estimate is published on the last working day of the month to which the figures relate, or shortly thereafter. 

The new indices are usually published between the first and second Thursday of the month following the reporting month. 

All CPI publication dates are shown in the publication calendar (see paragraph 3).

GENERAL INFORMATION This table contains figures on the Netherlands’ consumer price index (CPI). The CPI measures changes in the prices of goods and services purchased by households in the Netherlands for their own consumption. The table provides information about indices, monthly rates of change, annual rates of change and weighting coefficients. The annual rate of change of the CPI all items is known as the inflation. In addition to figures on total expenditure, figures on detailed product groups (expenditure categories) are also published. The table shows how much households in the Netherlands spend on each product group, on average, providing a picture of its share of total expenditure. This is also referred to as the weighting coefficient. The total weighting of the CPI is 100,000. The table also shows the derived CPI. This is the CPI that excludes the effect of changes in the rates of product-related taxes (e.g., VAT or excise taxes). As such, the price index approximates what the price change would be if tax rates had remained the same. CPI figures are published every month. After the end of each calendar year, annual figures are also released. The index figure for a given calendar year is calculated as the average of the indices for the twelve months in that year. Data available from: December 2009. Status of the figures: Provisional figures for each reporting month are published in a flash estimate. The flash estimate includes monthly and annual rates of change in the total CPI and in a number of main groups (special aggregates). These figures are based on source data that is not yet complete and cannot be used for indexation purposes. Therefore, no indices are published in the flash estimate. The figures used for the flash estimate are provisional. The flash estimate is followed by the first publication of indices and the rates of change across all expenditure categories. These figures are also provisional. The final figures for the same reporting month are published one month later. Any differences between the provisional and final figures are due to additional source data. Changes compared to the previous version include: Data for a new period has been added and/or adjustments have been made. When will new figures be published? The flash estimate is published on the last working day of the month to which the figures relate, or shortly thereafter. The new indices are usually published between the first and second Thursday of the month following the reporting month. All CPI publication dates are shown in the publication calendar (see paragraph 3). 2. DEFINITIONS AND EXPLANATION OF SYMBOLS Definitions: Consumer price index (CPI): The CPI measures changes in the prices of goods and services purchased by households in the Netherlands for their own consumption. Derived CPI: This price index excludes any changes in the tax rates on certain products (e.g. VAT and excise taxes on alcohol and tobacco) as well as subsidies and consumption-related taxes (e.g. motor vehicle tax). Expenditure category: The CPI measures price changes over time across a large number of expenditure categories (product groups). The categories are divided into different levels of classification: divisions, groups, classes, subclasses and micro classes. The table also includes specific constituent categories of product groups (special aggregates). In the explanation of the categories, an abbreviation in parentheses is used to indicate whether the category includes durable goods (D), semi-durable goods (SD), non-durable goods (ND) or services (S). The abbreviation 'n.e.c.' means 'not elsewhere classified'. Index figure: The index figure represents the price level in a period relative to a reference period. The price change can be calculated using the indices from different periods, such as the monthly rate of change and annual rate of change. Monthly rate of change: The monthly rate of change is the average price change over one month. The monthly rate of change is measured as the change in the indices relative to the previous reporting month. Annual rate of change: The annual rate of change is the average price change over one year. The annual rate of change is measured as the change in the indices relative to the corresponding period of the previous reporting year. Weighting coefficient: This shows how much households in the Netherlands spend on each expenditure category, on average, providing a picture of its share of total expenditure. This is also referred to as the weighting coefficient. The total weighting of the CPI is 100,000. Monthly figure: The CPI is published every month. The index figure reflects the average price level for consumer products in the relevant reporting month. Annual figure: After the end of each calendar year, annual figures are released. The index figure for a given calendar year is calculated as the average of the indices for the twelve months in that year. CBS only publishes the figures pertaining to calendar years in this table, but an average index figure can be calculated in the same manner for any twelve-month period. Explanation of symbols: empty cell : figure not applicable . : figure is unknown, insufficiently reliable or confidential * : provisional figures ** : more detailed provisional figures Indices are rounded to two decimal places. Monthly and annual rates of change are rounded to one decimal place. The weighting coefficients are rounded to a whole number. 3. LINKS TO RELEVANT TABLES AND ARTICLES Relevant tables: Consumer price index (CPI) since 1963, annual rate of change Consumer price index (CPI) 2025=100, contribution and impact Consumer price index (CPI) 2025=100, twelve-month average Consumer price index (CPI) 1900=100, index and annual rate of change European harmonised index of consumer prices (HICP) 2025=100, index and rates of change European harmonised index of consumer prices (HICP) 2025=100, index and annual rate of change in Europe Relevant articles: The dashboard on consumer prices shows charts on the CPI, the HICP and inflation: Dashboard on consumer prices. More information can be found on the theme page Prices. All CPI publication dates are shown in the publication calendar. 4. SOURCES AND METHODS The research method used for the CPI can be found in the brief survey description CPI 2025=100. More background information on the CPI is available in the comprehensive description for the CPI (only available in Dutch). See the classification used for the categorisation of the goods and services package: ECOICOPv2 classification (only available in Dutch). Flash estimate: The flash estimate is published on the last working day of the month to which the figures relate, or shortly thereafter. Monthly and annual rate of changes are published for the main CPI as well as for a number of specific constituent categories such as services, energy and food. This is in line with Eurostat's publication schedule for the European harmonised index of consumer prices (HICP). The source data used for the flash estimate is not yet complete, which means that the flash estimate cannot be used for indexation purposes. New base year for the CPI with effect from 2026: Effective 2026, the CPI and the HICP have moved to a new base year, from 2015=100 to 2025=100. An update of the classification of goods and services has also come into use in 2026, to reflect current consumption patterns better. Moreover, the CPI is brought more into line with the HICP from 2026 onwards. More information can be found in this long-read article on The consumer price index from 2026. Coronavirus pandemic between 2020 and 2022: Due to government measures to prevent the spread of coronavirus, sales of a number of goods and services were temporarily halted between 16 March 2020 and 25 January 2022. As a result, there were no or limited transactions by which prices could be measured for these goods and services and prices therefore had to be estimated. More information about the statistical implications of the coronavirus pandemic for calculating the CPI can be found via the links below: The impact of the coronavirus pandemic on compiling the CPI The impact of the coronavirus pandemic on the CPI weighting scheme (only available in Dutch) 5.
